capabilities.title: Whole-Article Markdown, HTML, DOCX and RTF import and export
capabilities.contract: Authors explicitly save whole current Draft content or load Markdown, HTML, DOCX and RTF into independent Articles through the existing Article header and Library file actions. Desktop export selects the format in the native Save As file-type dropdown; browser export uses a format dialog. Library export captures the targeted Article's working Draft without changing the open Article. Revisions exports complete saved Revision snapshots. Text highlighting never restricts export. Non-Markdown import requires a supported-content review before creation. Conversion preserves supported paragraphs, headings, nested editable lists and numbering, inline marks, safe links, quotes, code and Unicode; complex layouts simplify and embedded resources are omitted. Conversion is local with no Office requirement or remote resource loading. Imported titles use a leading level-one heading or the filename. Both runtimes enforce a 10 MiB file limit, safe names, strict UTF-8 for text formats, silent cancellation, and localized actionable failures. DOCX inflated parts and RTF nesting are bounded; worker-based imports have a deadline. Electron paths remain in main behind a finite validated sender-bound bridge and expiring single-use format tickets; saves replace destinations only after successful temporary writes. Browser export initiates a browser-managed download without claiming disk-write completion. The Copy menu and Revision restoration remain unchanged.
capabilities.persistence: Import checkpoints the previous Draft before creating one new independently recoverable Article and initial immutable Revision. Export creates no Revision and changes no Article or Draft. Paths are neither accepted from the renderer nor persisted.

capabilities.title: Immutable Revision timeline and read-only preview
capabilities.contract: The timeline and compact Status Bar selector distinguish initial, manual, AI-assisted, and restored Revisions. Revision history mutes and labels Revisions bypassed by the current restore path as Inactive, including the mobile selector; they remain selectable and restorable, and restoring one recalculates the active path. Conversational Assistant edits use the AI-assisted presentation and retain request and reply provenance. When the first immutable Revision is empty, the UI labels it Empty Revision and labels the second saved Revision Initial Revision; both remain selectable. New author, accepted-Proposal, and Assistant-edit Revisions use a concise configured-model summary of the changed context in the interface locale as their accessible history title, with a deterministic local fallback when generation fails or is cancelled. Selecting a Revision is local-only, opens a read-only preview, and does not alter the Article or Draft; restoration keeps the existing confirmation flow, and revision conflicts use an application contract rather than persistence types.
capabilities.persistence: Revisions are immutable local records ordered by creation. New content-changing Revisions persist their generated or fallback description only after completion; existing Revision records remain unchanged.

capabilities.title: Restore a prior Revision
capabilities.contract: Restoring a prior Revision creates a new Revision and never rewrites history; uncommitted Drafts require an explicit choice, and stale revision conflicts remain application-owned.
capabilities.persistence: Restoration appends a new immutable local Revision.

capabilities.title: Versioned local writing samples and explicit compact style profile rebuild
capabilities.contract: Authors manage included local samples, explicitly confirmed immutable Revision snapshots, and global rules; duplicate text is rejected and removal requires confirmation. For explicitly submitted text without a source name, the configured text-generation model names the sample while Submit shows loading. Input changes leave the current profile visible but outdated until explicit rebuild creates a version and Assistant service message. The profile identifies exact contributors and rebuild time.
capabilities.persistence: Raw samples, immutable Article Revision provenance, global rules, Article-specific rules, generated source names, and append-only compact profile versions remain local; Style Profile exposes a short local sample excerpt for author recognition.

capabilities.title: Revision-tied findings, citations, uncertainty, and stale indication
capabilities.contract: Findings remain advisory, Revision-tied, cited, uncertain, stale-aware, and actionable from Fact Check or Assistant. Fact Check defaults to the current Revision and lets Authors inspect retained runs by reviewed Revision and check date. It shows status badges, selected-finding navigation, original checked Revision and time for reused evidence, source dates, and independently scrolling navigation and detail panes. Older Revision and earlier same-Revision runs remain readable but read-only. Dated evidence carries a separate freshness reminder and refreshes only on explicit recheck. Accepting a finding records only local advisory resolution and creates no Revision. Only accepting a complete server-verified correction Proposal marks its selected findings corrected or removed in the same transaction as the new immutable Revision; dismissal, partial acceptance, and Revision conflict leave findings unresolved.
capabilities.persistence: Durable Facts, separate occurrences, findings, citations, and resolutions persist locally without modifying Article text; focused updates to other editorial artifacts do not replace or detach their citations.

capabilities.title: Linked translation Articles with source freshness protection
capabilities.contract: Translations are independently recoverable linked Articles. The workspace confirms selected target-language requests through Assistant messages, restores all completed unrejected proposals by identity, and supports language and result navigation. Repeated same-language generation on an unchanged source keeps earlier results and the source Revision. Each completed proposal contains the translated title and body; source and translation titles remain independent. Source Articles navigate linked translations through language tabs and Edit; each translation links back and identifies the source Revision. Edit opens an existing Article instead of creating a same-language duplicate. Edit, Update, and Reject are grouped above the tabs; the target name appears only in Update confirmation. Source and translation appear with full language names side by side, with paragraph and Markdown-list alignment where possible, plus visible protected-span validation and stale-source warnings. A proposal with changed or missing protected content cannot create a translation Article. The selected translation shows advisory character guidance for the Article's selected publishing profile. Created translations open in the editor for author-controlled Drafts and Revisions; stale proposals cannot create them. Authors can explicitly reject an exact generated result after confirmation, which removes only that result from approval without changing the source, sibling results, or accepted translation history. Freshness is displayed for the selected proposal and when an accepted translation is opened. An explicitly confirmed refresh accepts a validated completed source artifact into a named existing translation, appending a Revision and updating its source link atomically while preserving its title, siblings, and prior history. Source or target conflicts, retained target Drafts, rejected artifacts, and invalid or mismatched output prevent refresh. Restoring earlier translation text also restores its source snapshot.
capabilities.persistence: All completed and rejected translation proposals persist in local Assistant artifacts. Repeated same-language results recover by stable artifact or message identity, with generation time and source Revision. Rejecting one result preserves siblings and accepted history; Source Article and Revision linkage persist on the independently recoverable translation Article.

capabilities.title: Explicit Markdown and plain-text copying with character guidance
capabilities.contract: The Status Bar main action copies current Article Markdown, while its menu offers Markdown or deterministically prepared plain text. Article-specific profile guidance, including configured custom profiles, remains available beside it. Copying is explicit and direct publishing is not performed.
capabilities.persistence: Copied output is derived from the local Article and locally persisted profile data.

capabilities.title: Named profiles with configurable limits
capabilities.contract: Authors choose a predefined default for new Articles and configure named custom non-negative limits with stable IDs. Each Article independently selects Default, No restrictions, LinkedIn Post, LinkedIn Article, or a custom profile for advisory guidance.
capabilities.persistence: The default profile and custom name/limit persist locally in app_settings.publish-limit-profile; Article-specific selection persists locally.

scenarios.title: File import creates an independent recoverable Article after review
preconditions: The Author has a current Article and chooses Load from file.
scenarios.event: The Author imports a supported file, cancels the picker or review, or encounters a conversion/checkpoint failure.
expected: Valid Markdown creates a separate Article through the application client with a heading or filename title; both Articles recover after reload.
Cancellation and failures preserve the current Article and its Draft.
forbidden: Implicitly overwriting an existing Article or creating a new Article after a failed Draft checkpoint.

scenarios.title: File save exports whole Draft content without changing history
preconditions: The Author opens a current Article with highlighted text.
scenarios.event: The Author saves Markdown, cancels, or encounters a file-write error.
expected: The complete current workspace Markdown is exported, and success/failure feedback is localized.
Cancellation is silent and export creates no Revision.
The Library context menu and header tooltips show Save to file… and Load from file…. The Library menu separates file actions from Article management actions.
forbidden: Exporting only the highlighted text or changing Article history.

scenarios.title: Native text and binary file operations remain bounded and authorized
preconditions: The Author uses the Electron file client.
scenarios.event: The client loads/saves selected file bytes, cancels, sends an invalid request, or encounters a replacement failure.
expected: The client round-trips UTF-8 Markdown and binary bytes through native file operations with four file-type filters.
Save tickets are single-use, format-bound and invalidated on navigation; destination paths never reach the renderer.
Cancelled operations are no-ops, invalid senders/requests never open dialogs, failures return only safe codes, and failed replacement preserves prior data.
forbidden: Renderer-selected filesystem paths, private details in errors, or destination truncation before a successful write.

scenarios.title: Local format conversion preserves basic editable structure
preconditions: A supported file contains paragraphs, lists, inline marks and Unicode.
scenarios.event: The local converters import or export HTML, DOCX or RTF.
expected: Basic content and editable nested lists retain their structure and numbering starts.
Executable markup and embedded resources are omitted, malformed files fail safely, and actual inflated data and parser nesting are bounded.
forbidden: Remote resource fetching, executing imported content, or accepting unbounded parser input.

scenarios.title: Revision history is browsable without changing Article content
preconditions: An Article has initial and subsequent Revisions.
scenarios.event: The author selects an earlier Revision in history.
expected: A formatted read-only preview and distinct provenance timeline icon are shown.
Revisions bypassed by the current restore path are muted and labeled Inactive while remaining available to preview and restore.
forbidden: Selecting history alters the current Article or Draft.

scenarios.title: Restoring preserves immutable Revision history
preconditions: An author has selected an earlier Revision.
expected: The restore request identifies the selected Revision and the repository creates a new Revision.

scenarios.title: New content Revisions retain concise descriptions
preconditions: An author explicitly saves or accepts changed Article content.
scenarios.event: The configured text-generation model completes, fails, or is cancelled while the Revision is being created.
expected: A successful concise description is stored with the new Revision; otherwise a deterministic local fallback is stored and the accepted content remains recoverable.
forbidden: Changing existing Revision records, blocking Revision creation after model failure, or sending unchanged Article context to the model.

scenarios.title: Assistant edit Revisions have generated descriptions
preconditions: An explicit Assistant edit has a valid replacement for the Article or its selection.
scenarios.event: The edit is applied directly or from its completed reply.
expected: The new immutable Revision stores a concise description generated from the changed context in the interface locale; generation failure uses the existing local fallback.
forbidden: A fixed Assistant edit title replacing an available generated description, duplicate Revisions on repeated Apply, or a description update to an older Revision.

scenarios.title: Style corpus stays local while a compact profile is derived
preconditions: The author adds a writing sample, optionally without a source name.
scenarios.event: The style corpus or global rules change.
expected: A submitted blank source name is generated with the configured text model; a confirmed Article Revision snapshot retains its source Revision; removing a sample requires confirmation; the current profile is marked outdated until an explicit rebuild creates the next compact version, and the rebuild is recorded in the selected Article's Assistant chat.
forbidden: Treating raw style samples as remote application data outside the author-explicit name-generation request.

scenarios.title: Fact findings remain advisory and Revision-tied
preconditions: The author requests a fact check for the current Revision.
expected: Findings retain source citations, uncertainty, and the reviewed Revision identifier.

scenarios.title: Retained Fact Check runs remain readable by Revision
preconditions: Fact Check runs exist for current and earlier Revisions.
scenarios.event: The Author chooses a retained run in Fact Check history.
expected: The chosen run shows only its own findings, check dates, and source dates.
Historical runs are read-only and rechecking is explicit.
forbidden: Historical findings creating corrections or modifying Article text.

scenarios.title: Exact translation artifact acceptance preserves siblings and rejects removed results
preconditions: Two same-Revision and same-language artifacts are completed.
scenarios.event: The Author creates an independent Article or refreshes a target using an older result, then rejects its sibling.
expected: Accepted content and provenance use the exact artifact. Target history and sibling proposals remain preserved. Rejected artifacts, including legacy message-only rejection, cannot create or refresh Articles.
forbidden: Acceptance of rejected content or rewriting accepted history.

scenarios.title: Repeated same-language proposals recover independently
preconditions: Two completed results exist for the same source Revision and language.
scenarios.event: The Workspace reloads and the Author rejects one selected result.
expected: Both results are selectable after reload. Rejection removes only the named artifact and preserves its sibling.
forbidden: Collapsing completed proposals by language or rewriting accepted history.

scenarios.title: Stale source content blocks linked translation creation
preconditions: A translation proposal's source Revision is stale.
expected: The stale-source warning is shown.
forbidden: Creating a translation Article from stale source content.

scenarios.title: Editing the source marks linked translations stale without changing their text
preconditions: The source Article has independently accepted Spanish and German translations.
scenarios.event: The Author saves a new source Revision and opens Translations.
expected: Linked translations retain their text and Revision IDs and show Outdated; each translation warns when opened.
forbidden: Automatic translation changes or false freshness.

scenarios.title: Explicit translation refresh preserves history and source provenance atomically
preconditions: A valid current source translation proposal and an existing linked target are available.
scenarios.event: The Author confirms acceptance into the named target translation.
expected: Acceptance appends one Revision and updates the source link; restoring an older translation Revision restores its source freshness. Legacy history remains unchanged.
forbidden: Overwriting history, losing a Draft, accepting a stale source or target, or changing siblings.

scenarios.title: Header copy offers Markdown and plain text without direct publishing
preconditions: The current Article has a selected publishing profile.
scenarios.event: The author uses the Status Bar Copy control.
expected: The main action copies Markdown and the menu offers deterministic plain text without AI.

scenarios.title: Publishing profile selection persists locally
preconditions: A publishing default and custom profile name/limit are configured.
scenarios.event: The service saves and reloads that selection.
expected: The selected default and valid custom profile configuration are returned after reload.
forbidden: Accepting unknown profiles or invalid custom limits.
